other: {"answer":"Errors propagate through two layers: the per-request `dispatch()` recursion inside `compose()` (src/compose.ts), and a final catch-all in `#dispatch()` in src/hono-base.ts. The key subtlety is that errors are caught at the *innermost* dispatch level that has a `try/catch`, not necessarily at the outermost middleware — so custom try/catch blocks written inside outer middleware around `next()` typically never see downstream errors, because the framework's `onError` swallows them first.

Detailed path:

1. In `compose()`, each recursive call `dispatch(i)` wraps `res = await handler(context, () => dispatch(i+1))` in its own try/catch. `onError` is a single closure variable shared by every recursion level (it's the `errorHandler` passed once into `compose(...)`), not per-middleware.
2. If a handler throws (synchronously or via an awaited rejection) at level i+1, that throw happens inside dispatch(i+1)'s own try/catch (the frame closest to the actual throw), not the caller's. Since `onError` is defined (Hono always supplies a default `errorHandler` — src/hono-base.ts lines 36-42 — unless overridden by `app.onError()`, line 272), dispatch(i+1) catches it immediately: sets `context.error = err`, calls `res = await onError(err, context)`, sets `isError = true`, and returns normally (no rethrow). This means the promise returned to the outer middleware's `await next()` resolves normally — outer middleware code after `next()` still runs, but any try/catch it wrapped around `next()` never fires, since the error was already absorbed downstream.
3. If `onError` is NOT supplied to a given `compose()` call, the catch block's condition `err instanceof Error && onError` is false, so it does `throw err` instead — letting the error keep bubbling as a rejected promise to whatever awaits that `compose()` invocation. This actually happens in practice: `every()` in src/middleware/combine/index.ts calls `compose(middleware.map(...))` with no `onError`/`onNotFound` arguments at all, so any thrown "Unmet condition" or user middleware error rethrows out of that inner compose, through `every`'s async function, and up into whatever outer compose/dispatch is running it (which does have the real `errorHandler`).
4. At the top, `#dispatch()` in hono-base.ts (~line 449-464) calls `compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)` and wraps the whole `await composed(c)` call in a try/catch that calls `this.#handleError(err, c)` → `this.errorHandler(err, c)`. This is a last-resort net for errors that escape all of compose's own handling (e.g., non-`Error` throws just get rethrown by compose's catch condition, or errors from router matching/context construction outside compose).
5. `#handleError` (line 399-404) only calls `this.errorHandler` if `err instanceof Error`; otherwise it rethrows the raw value, which becomes an unhandled rejection at the fetch entrypoint.
6. Single-middleware routes (`matchResult[0].length === 1`, hono-base.ts ~415-447) skip `compose()` entirely and call the handler directly inside a plain try/catch / `.catch()`, invoking `this.#handleError` the same way — so the same error contract holds even on the fast path.
7. Errors propagate through two layers: the per-request `dispatch()` recursion inside `compose()` (src/compose.ts), and a final catch-all in `#dispatch()` in src/hono-base.ts. The key subtlety is that errors are caught at the *innermost* dispatch level that has a `try/catch`, not necessarily at the outermost middleware — so custom try/catch blocks written inside outer middleware around `next()` typically never see downstream errors, because the framework's `onError` swallows them first.

Detailed path:

1. In `compose()`, each recursive call `dispatch(i)` wraps `res = await handler(context, () => dispatch(i+1))` in its own try/catch. `onError` is a single closure variable shared by every recursion level (it's the `errorHandler` passed once into `compose(...)`), not per-middleware.
2. If a handler throws (synchronously or via an awaited rejection) at level i+1, that throw happens inside dispatch(i+1)'s own try/catch (the frame closest to the actual throw), not the caller's. Since `onError` is defined (Hono always supplies a default `errorHandler` — src/hono-base.ts lines 36-42 — unless overridden by `app.onError()`, line 272), dispatch(i+1) catches it immediately: sets `context.error = err`, calls `res = await onError(err, context)`, sets `isError = true`, and returns normally (no rethrow). This means the promise returned to the outer middleware's `await next()` resolves normally — outer middleware code after `next()` still runs, but any try/catch it wrapped around `next()` never fires, since the error was already absorbed downstream.
3. If `onError` is NOT supplied to a given `compose()` call, the catch block's condition `err instanceof Error && onError` is false, so it does `throw err` instead — letting the error keep bubbling as a rejected promise to whatever awaits that `compose()` invocation. This actually happens in practice: `every()` in src/middleware/combine/index.ts calls `compose(middleware.map(...))` with no `onError`/`onNotFound` arguments at all, so any thrown "Unmet condition" or user middleware error rethrows out of that inner compose, through `every`'s async function, and up into whatever outer compose/dispatch is running it (which does have the real `errorHandler`).
4. At the top, `#dispatch()` in hono-base.ts (~line 449-464) calls `compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)` and wraps the whole `await composed(c)` call in a try/catch that calls `this.#handleError(err, c)` → `this.errorHandler(err, c)`. This is a last-resort net for errors that escape all of compose's own handling (e.g., non-`Error` throws just get rethrown by compose's catch condition, or errors from router matching/context construction outside compose).
5. `#handleError` (line 399-404) only calls `this.errorHandler` if `err instanceof Error`; otherwise it rethrows the raw value, which becomes an unhandled rejection at the fetch entrypoint.
6. Single-middleware routes (`matchResult[0].length === 1`, hono-base.ts ~415-447) skip `compose()` entirely and call the handler directly inside a plain try/catch / `.catch()`, invoking `this.#handleError` the same way — so the same error contract holds even on the fast path.
7. Edge case: if the user's `onError` handler itself throws inside compose's catch block, that new exception is not further guarded at that level and propagates up the dispatch chain; if it reaches the very top, `#dispatch`'s outer catch invokes `this.errorHandler` a second time on it, which can throw again in a genuinely unguarded way.
8. `NotFoundHandler` follows an analogous but separate path — triggered when `handler` is `undefined` for index i and `context.finalized === false` — it is not part of the error-catching branch.

report.answer:
Errors propagate through two layers: the per-request `dispatch()` recursion inside `compose()` (src/compose.ts), and a final catch-all in `#dispatch()` in src/hono-base.ts. The key subtlety is that errors are caught at the *innermost* dispatch level that has a `try/catch`, not necessarily at the outermost middleware — so custom try/catch blocks written inside outer middleware around `next()` typically never see downstream errors, because the framework's `onError` swallows them first.

Detailed path:

1. In `compose()`, each recursive call `dispatch(i)` wraps `res = await handler(context, () => dispatch(i+1))` in its own try/catch. `onError` is a single closure variable shared by every recursion level (it's the `errorHandler` passed once into `compose(...)`), not per-middleware.
2. If a handler throws (synchronously or via an awaited rejection) at level i+1, that throw happens inside dispatch(i+1)'s own try/catch (the frame closest to the actual throw), not the caller's. Since `onError` is defined (Hono always supplies a default `errorHandler` — src/hono-base.ts lines 36-42 — unless overridden by `app.onError()`, line 272), dispatch(i+1) catches it immediately: sets `context.error = err`, calls `res = await onError(err, context)`, sets `isError = true`, and returns normally (no rethrow). This means the promise returned to the outer middleware's `await next()` resolves normally — outer middleware code after `next()` still runs, but any try/catch it wrapped around `next()` never fires, since the error was already absorbed downstream.
3. If `onError` is NOT supplied to a given `compose()` call, the catch block's condition `err instanceof Error && onError` is false, so it does `throw err` instead — letting the error keep bubbling as a rejected promise to whatever awaits that `compose()` invocation. This actually happens in practice: `every()` in src/middleware/combine/index.ts calls `compose(middleware.map(...))` with no `onError`/`onNotFound` arguments at all, so any thrown "Unmet condition" or user middleware error rethrows out of that inner compose, through `every`'s async function, and up into whatever outer compose/dispatch is running it (which does have the real `errorHandler`).
4. At the top, `#dispatch()` in hono-base.ts (~line 449-464) calls `compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)` and wraps the whole `await composed(c)` call in a try/catch that calls `this.#handleError(err, c)` → `this.errorHandler(err, c)`. This is a last-resort net for errors that escape all of compose's own handling (e.g., non-`Error` throws just get rethrown by compose's catch condition, or errors from router matching/context construction outside compose).
5. `#handleError` (line 399-404) only calls `this.errorHandler` if `err instanceof Error`; otherwise it rethrows the raw value, which becomes an unhandled rejection at the fetch entrypoint.
6. Single-middleware routes (`matchResult[0].length === 1`, hono-base.ts ~415-447) skip `compose()` entirely and call the handler directly inside a plain try/catch / `.catch()`, invoking `this.#handleError` the same way — so the same error contract holds even on the fast path.
7. Edge case: if the user's `onError` handler itself throws inside compose's catch block, that new exception is not further guarded at that level and propagates up the dispatch chain; if it reaches the very top, `#dispatch`'s outer catch invokes `this.errorHandler` a second time on it, which can throw again in a genuinely unguarded way.
8. `NotFoundHandler` follows an analogous but separate path — triggered when `handler` is `undefined` for index i and `context.finalized === false` — it is not part of the error-catching branch.

report.answer:
Errors propagate through two layers: the per-request `dispatch()` recursion inside `compose()` (src/compose.ts), and a final catch-all in `#dispatch()` in src/hono-base.ts. The key subtlety is that errors are caught at the *innermost* dispatch level that has a `try/catch`, not necessarily at the outermost middleware — so custom try/catch blocks written inside outer middleware around `next()` typically never see downstream errors, because the framework's `onError` swallows them first.

Detailed path:

1. In `compose()`, each recursive call `dispatch(i)` wraps `res = await handler(context, () => dispatch(i+1))` in its own try/catch. `onError` is a single closure variable shared by every recursion level (it's the `errorHandler` passed once into `compose(...)`), not per-middleware.
2. If a handler throws (synchronously or via an awaited rejection) at level i+1, that throw happens inside dispatch(i+1)'s own try/catch (the frame closest to the actual throw), not the caller's. Since `onError` is defined (Hono always supplies a default `errorHandler` — src/hono-base.ts lines 36-42 — unless overridden by `app.onError()`, line 272), dispatch(i+1) catches it immediately: sets `context.error = err`, calls `res = await onError(err, context)`, sets `isError = true`, and returns normally (no rethrow). This means the promise returned to the outer middleware's `await next()` resolves normally — outer middleware code after `next()` still runs, but any try/catch it wrapped around `next()` never fires, since the error was already absorbed downstream.
3. If `onError` is NOT supplied to a given `compose()` call, the catch block's condition `err instanceof Error && onError` is false, so it does `throw err` instead — letting the error keep bubbling as a rejected promise to whatever awaits that `compose()` invocation. This actually happens in practice: `every()` in src/middleware/combine/index.ts calls `compose(middleware.map(...))` with no `onError`/`onNotFound` arguments at all, so any thrown "Unmet condition" or user middleware error rethrows out of that inner compose, through `every`'s async function, and up into whatever outer compose/dispatch is running it (which does have the real `errorHandler`).
4. At the top, `#dispatch()` in hono-base.ts (~line 449-464) calls `compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)` and wraps the whole `await composed(c)` call in a try/catch that calls `this.#handleError(err, c)` → `this.errorHandler(err, c)`. This is a last-resort net for errors that escape all of compose's own handling (e.g., non-`Error` throws just get rethrown by compose's catch condition, or errors from router matching/context construction outside compose).
5. `#handleError` (line 399-404) only calls `this.errorHandler` if `err instanceof Error`; otherwise it rethrows the raw value, which becomes an unhandled rejection at the fetch entrypoint.
6. Single-middleware routes (`matchResult[0].length === 1`, hono-base.ts ~415-447) skip `compose()` entirely and call the handler directly inside a plain try/catch / `.catch()`, invoking `this.#handleError` the same way — so the same error contract holds even on the fast path.
7. Edge case: if the user's `onError` handler itself throws inside compose's catch block, that new exception is not further guarded at that level and propagates up the dispatch chain; if it reaches the very top, `#dispatch`'s outer catch invokes `this.errorHandler` a second time on it, which can throw again in a genuinely unguarded way.
8. `NotFoundHandler` follows an analogous but separate path — triggered when `handler` is `undefined` for index i and `context.finalized === false` — it is not part of the error-catching branch.
